b: p
Have you ever had a chronically unreliable partner? Did you find a solution other than breaking up?
p
I'm looking for advice because I feel completely stuck in my marriage.
p

We've been together for over 10 years, we're married, and we have two children. My husband is handsome, intelligent, sensitive, loving, and artistic. I've never felt the same kind of attraction or connection with anyone else. That's why I ignored all the red flags and built a life with him.
p
Now we've settled into a deeply unhappy dynamic where I feel like a single parent to three children, except one of them is a teenager who happens to be my husband.
p

I carry the entire mental load, do most of the housework, and take care of the kids. I'm the CEO of our family. My husband is an unpaid intern. I'm also the only one with a steady job, since my husband only works occasional temporary jobs. So most of the time we live on one income, which adds even more stress and makes everyday life harder.
p

My husband is probably neurodivergent, and he had a traumatic childhood. Even before we met, he was barely managing to keep his life together. He was constantly late paying rent, didn't have a job, regularly missed doctor's appointments and other commitments, and his home looked more like a cluttered storage unit than an actual place to live.
p

At first, I hoped he would change. He hasn't, at least not in the ways that matter most to our everyday life. To be fair, he has made progress in other areas during our marriage. He's worked through some of his childhood trauma and got a new degree and profession.
p
I know what most reasonable people are probably thinking at this point: just leave. He's not my responsibility.
p

But I genuinely don't believe he would be able to get back on his feet if we separated. I think he would most likely fall apart completely. There's a very real possibility that he might take his own life. I understand that his choices are not my responsibility, but that doesn't make the possibility any less real.
p
Some of you are probably wondering why I've stayed this long.
p

At his best, my husband is incredibly affectionate, loving, and caring. He patiently listens to my worries and does lots of small, thoughtful things to show his love. He's deeply committed to me, and I've never had to worry about his loyalty or faithfulness.
p

Our children love him because, at his best, he's a fun and engaged father. We've shared a kind of emotional intimacy, friendship, and almost soulmate-like connection that I know is incredibly hard to find. I believe my husband would take a bullet for me.
p

But not the dishes, apparently. The problem is simply trying to run a household and raise a family with him. When it comes to the practical responsibilities of everyday life, he contributes very little.
p
To his credit, he does try.
p

We've sat down and talked about these problems countless times. I've explained how overwhelmed, exhausted, and disappointed I feel. He listens, even though I can see how much it hurts him to hear these things.
p

Usually, after one of these conversations, things improve for a couple of weeks. He does more chores, makes an effort, and tries to take responsibility. Then, before long, we're right back where we started.
p

I've also tried simply stepping back and letting things go undone. But the result is that the bills don't get paid, the kids don't get fed, and dirty dishes sit around until they grow mold. Eventually, I give in and start taking care of everything again.
p
We've divided up responsibilities and made very clear agreements about who is supposed to do what, many times. But no system seems to work with him because he simply doesn't follow through.
p

If he's responsible for something important, it doesn't matter how many times I remind him or emphasize how absolutely essential it is that he gets it done. There's still a good chance he'll be fast asleep when he should already be on his way.
p
The result is that I can't rely on him for anything, big or small. I always need a backup plan in case he doesn't follow through.
p
I think about leaving quite often, but several things hold me back.
p
First, I know a separation would be devastating for our children.
p
Second, I don't know if I could live with myself if my husband ended up homeless or died by suicide.
p

Third, I have a disability that makes me feel my chances of finding another partner would be limited. There's a very real possibility that I would end up alone. And I wonder whether having a "partner" who at least does something is still better than having no partner at all.
p
And of course, I would miss the good parts of our relationship terribly. The closeness, the affection, the friendship, and all the moments when things actually feel wonderful between us.
p
But everyday life is so exhausting that sometimes I honestly wonder how much longer I can keep going.
p
I dream about having a real partner, someone I could share responsibilities with, someone I could actually depend on. I feel jealous of people who have equal, reliable partners.
p
At the same time, I know I got myself into this situation. I ignored the warning signs because I naively believed my husband was capable of becoming someone who could handle more responsibility.
p
I feel like I've tried just about everything, but I keep wondering if there's something I haven't thought of.
p
Has anyone here been in a similar relationship and actually found a way to make it work without separating? Has anyone managed to stop being their spouse's life manager?
p
If you did, what changed? What finally helped? And looking back, what advice would you give someone in my position?
p
I'm especially interested in hearing from people who have actually lived through something similar, whether you stayed together or eventually separated. Thank you in advance for any insight.
p
Note: English isn't my first language, so I used AI to help translate and polish my own original text.
p

TL;DR: My husband is loving and affectionate but chronically unreliable. I handle almost all the household, childcare, and financial responsibilities, and nothing we've tried has led to lasting change. I'm exhausted but still love him deeply and fear the consequences of leaving. Has anyone found a way to make a relationship like this work?
